correctness.rationale: The finite metric has 2M extreme directed edge molecules. A polytope edge is exactly a two-vertex exposed face. Common-head/tail pairs admit the explicit 0,1,1/2 support potential; consecutive pairs force a difference of 2 and an additional tight edge because there are at least three parts. For disjoint pairs the cross inequalities force delta=0 when both cross graph edges exist; absence of either permits a strict 1/2-offset construction. This proves the complete iff adjacency rule. Each pair of original edges whose part-pairs intersect has exactly one oriented adjacent lift per fiber; hence the 2-cover structure. Exact inclusion–exclusion gives degree N(a+b)-a²-ab-b²-1. For tripartite graphs this equals M-1; with >=4 parts the difference (b-c)(N-a-b-c) forces equality of all part sizes for regularity. The fiber-constant Laplacian is MI-J, so eigenvalue M has multiplicity at least M-1. Both standalone scripts were inspected in their actual new-package directory and successfully executed: nine complete pairwise LP checks, five independent convex hull rank checks, degree and cover checks. Numerical tests are not used to infer universal validity.

originality.rationale: Aliaga–Pernecká classifies individual extreme molecules, not adjacency between them. The 2018 multipartite literature enumerates facets; the 2019 face-poset result treats cycles; 2023 matroid theory asserts unimodular equivalence and facet descriptions. The directly closest complete-bipartite two-cover result fixes two metric parts, and cannot imply the all-tripartite and at-least-four-part degree-regularity dichotomy merely by substituting parameters: triangle-containing graphs are not graph-matroid equivalent to bipartite graphs. Seven semantic published-finding corpus searches, relevant primary full-text passages and several web literature searches yielded no evaluated multipartite k>=3 one-skeleton covering/degrees/regularity theorem. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a guarantee of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named evaluation of a complete multipartite 1-skeleton might exist.

General matroidal or triangulation statements may facilitate an independent derivation, but the located sources do not explicitly imply the all-parameter evaluated degree/regularity theorem without the present analysis.
Some low-dimensional, complete-graph and bipartite graph special cases have previous coverage; novelty is the unified k>=3 classification and k=3 versus k>=4 regularity boundary.

value.rationale: This determines all one-dimensional face adjacencies for every unit complete multipartite metric with >=3 parts, a natural Banach-ball invariant not reducible to a known facet count. The graph is represented as an explicit antipodal signed double cover of a weighted clique blow-up of the line graph of K_k. A genuine structural transition appears: every arbitrarily unbalanced three-part metric has a regular skeleton on 2M vertices with M(M-1) edges, whereas four or more parts require exact balance to be regular. The forced (M-1)-dimensional Laplacian eigenspace adds a reproducible spectral consequence. The novelty concerns a family-wide qualitative feature and explicit formula, not a routine renaming of a known bipartite special case.
